gaps.issue: 4 routed net(s) look like high-speed interfaces by their name but have no target impedance (their net class has none). Name-based: confirm before acting.
gaps.where_to_find: Interface standard or the device datasheets (e.g. 85/90/100 Ω differential). Nets in the class “Default” need their own net class in KiCad first (Board Setup → Net Classes, or net class directives in the schematic) – kisi.json can only set values of existing classes.

gaps.issue: 5 dielectric layer(s) carry default or missing material data.
gaps.where_to_find: Laminate datasheet of the named material (εr and tanδ near the signal frequencies, e.g. 1–10 GHz, for the resin content / glass style of this layer), or the fabricator's stackup report. Mark typical values as such.

gaps.issue: 4 net class(es) with a target impedance get only a generic profile (no data rate / standard): the channel check uses 1 Gbit/s and generic limits.
gaps.where_to_find: What runs on these nets: schematic (bus names, the devices at the ends: `kisi interfaces`) and the device datasheets (interface, data rate). Available profiles: `kisi profiles`.

gaps.issue: 1 supply rail(s) without a known voltage (found by their name, a pin name such as VBUS, VSYS, VBAT, VDD, or a field): kisi needs the voltage to put their loads and sources into the power tree, the budget and the IR drop. Found by name: confirm that each one is a supply.
gaps.where_to_find: Schematic: the regulator, load switch or connector that feeds the rail and its output voltage (regulator datasheet / voltage setting, USB VBUS 5 V, battery nominal voltage). A rail behind a ferrite, a 0 Ω link or a shunt takes the voltage of the rail before it.

source.note: VSYS follows VBUS while USB is present

write.note: Write the voltage where the rail appears in PI_REG: as the output of the part that feeds it (`+5V > VSYS@5V buck 90%`) or as a supply input (`VBAT@3.7V input`). Behind a ferrite, 0 Ω link or shunt use a pass element (`+3V3 > IMU_VDD pass r=0.5`: the voltage carries over; items[].write suggests it when kisi finds such a part). Net names with spaces in double quotes (`"/Power/VDD CORE"@0.9V`). Without a power tree: PI_SOURCE `NAME=<V>V` on the source part. Nets that are not supplies: ignore.
write.to: fields[] – the rail with its voltage as NAME@<V>V in a PI_REG entry

gaps.issue: 7 IC(s) on supply rails have no load current (field PI_LOAD): their current is missing from IR drop and budget.
gaps.where_to_find: Device datasheets (look up the mpn when an item has one: the Value field is not always the part number): supply current per rail in the expected operating mode (state typical or maximum in the source note); FPGAs/SoCs: the vendor's power estimator.

gaps.issue: 256 decoupling capacitor(s) of 100 nF and more have no rated voltage or dielectric: the DC-bias derating in Z(f) uses an assumed rating.
gaps.where_to_find: BOM / capacitor datasheet: rated voltage, dielectric (X5R/X7R/C0G), ideally the capacitance at the rail voltage from the vendor's DC-bias curve, ESR and ESL.

write.to: fields[] (name PI_CAP) or the KiCad Value field (e.g. 10u 6.3V X5R)

gaps.issue: 14 part(s) dissipate 0.1 W or more without thermal data (field PI_THERMAL): `kisi thermal` estimates their junction temperature from package defaults and assumes Tj max 125 °C.
gaps.where_to_find: Device datasheet: the Thermal Information table (RθJB, RθJC(top) – or ψJB – for the JEDEC 2s2p board) and the maximum junction temperature (Absolute Maximum Ratings / Recommended Operating Conditions). Heat that leaves the board (connectors, LEDs, RF output): p=<W>.

how: Fill the gaps in <board>.kisi.json next to the board (format: see `kisi config-template`), every value with a source; then run `kisi config-check <board>` and `kisi gaps <board>` again. Gaps marked 'not kisi.json' are fixes in KiCad.
